summary: FireLens turns three disagreeing NASA fire records into one fair, monthly burning calendar for 49 districts of Punjab, Haryana and Uttarakhand, from 2016 to 2026. Terra MODIS, Aqua MODIS and Suomi-NPP VIIRS see the same crop fires very differently (in Oct–Nov 2021: 3,766 vs 35,721 vs 28,679 hotspots), mainly because of their overpass times and sensitivity. We divide fire pixels by clearly seen pixels so clouds don't fake "no fire", scale MODIS to VIIRS with one ratio per state and calendar month, and blend the sensors, dropping MODIS after its orbit drift. Tested on years it never saw, scaled Terra and Aqua match VIIRS at r = 0.91 and 0.98. A free live web app lets farmers, researchers and policymakers see whether this month is unusual, follow trends, draw their own area and download the data. It matters because crop-residue burning drives North India's winter smog, and policy needs one trustworthy record, not three.
details:
WHAT IT DOES

FireLens is a live web app (https://harmonization-space-app-alvgdbyul5te9zfje6c3fz.streamlit.app/) that shows one harmonized, month-by-month burning-activity calendar for 49 districts of Punjab, Haryana and Uttarakhand, January 2016 to November 2026, built from three NASA satellites.

THE PROBLEM

Terra MODIS (~10:30 am pass), Aqua MODIS (~1:30 pm) and Suomi-NPP VIIRS (~1:30 pm) observe the same fires but report very different numbers. Terra's morning pass misses most afternoon crop burning, clouds hide whole monsoon months, and since 2022–2023 both MODIS orbits have drifted to different overpass times. Raw counts from different sensors cannot be compared year to year.

HOW IT WORKS

1. Collect: in Google Earth Engine, for every district, month and sensor we count fire pixels (FireMask ≥ 8) and clearly seen land pixels in the daily 1 km products.

2. Normalize: burning activity = fire pixels ÷ clearly seen pixels, so cloudy months are not mistaken for fire-free months. Months with no usable images are left blank, never zero.

3. Harmonize: Suomi-NPP VIIRS is the anchor (it covers the whole period). Terra and Aqua are scaled to it with one ratio per state and calendar month, fitted on 2016–2022, then blended with VIIRS, weighted by how well each predicted VIIRS in years it never saw. MODIS is used only from before its orbit drift (Terra from Oct 2022, Aqua from Feb 2023).

4. Validate: in a leave-one-year-out test, scaled Terra matches VIIRS at r = 0.91 and Aqua at r = 0.98, both within 4% of VIIRS's peak-season total; MODIS alone rebuilds the VIIRS record at r = 0.97 with a 2% bias. The calendar recovers the known seasons: Ludhiana's Oct–Nov rice-straw burning (4.3× its yearly average) and Naini Tal's Apr–May forest fires (3.9×).

WHAT USERS CAN DO

- Pick a district or type a latitude/longitude, choose any date range and the harmonized series or any single sensor.

- See a month × year calendar, yearly view, anomaly against each month's median, and sensor comparison before and after harmonization; every value shows the range of the three sensors.

- Metric cards: how the latest month compares with its usual level and its percentile rank.

- Trend tab: Mann-Kendall test with Sen's slope per district and as a map, with the MODIS drift years marked.

- Draw any box or polygon on the map to get that area's own calendar, trend and hotspot list.

- Fire-type view (cropland / forest / woodland, plus static heat sources) for 19 districts.

- Download harmonized and per-sensor monthly CSVs, individual hotspots (date, location, FRP, sensor), or everything as one ZIP with a data dictionary and citation file; every chart exports as PNG.

WHAT WE FOUND

Detected rice-season (Oct–Nov) hotspots across the 49 districts fell 96% from 2021 to 2025 (Suomi-NPP: 28,679 to 1,111), in line with the official CAQM count for Punjab (−93%). Later-passing Aqua still sees more, so part of the fall may be burning moved past the satellites' overpass; FireLens flags this rather than hiding it.

BENEFITS

Farmers and extension workers can see if this season is unusual; air-quality researchers get a clean, long fire series to compare with PM2.5; policymakers can see which districts burn most and whether it is improving, on one consistent scale.

LIMITATIONS AND NEXT STEPS

Values are detections of 1 km pixels, not counts of individual fires. Boundaries are FAO GAUL 2015, not official Indian boundaries. Suomi-NPP product delivery ended on 1 Nov 2026, so the next step is adding NOAA-20 and NOAA-21 VIIRS; we also plan to extend the calendar back to 2001 with MODIS, cover fire types for all 49 districts, and use official district boundaries.

TOOLS

Python (pandas, NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib), Google Earth Engine (JavaScript and Python), Streamlit, Plotly, Folium and streamlit-folium, pytest (135 automated tests), GitHub, Streamlit Community Cloud. Demo video made with Remotion.

AI USE

We used Claude (Anthropic) as a coding and writing assistant to help write and review parts of the data pipeline and app, write tests, draft documentation and build the demo video with Remotion; the team checked all science choices and results, which are reproducible from our repository. The demo video's voiceover is AI-generated with Kokoro TTS (open source); the video carries a visible "AI-assisted video · AI-generated voice" label, and this is also stated in the video file's metadata and the YouTube description. Charts, maps and numbers in the video are drawn by code from our real NASA data. No AI content uses or changes NASA branding.
